questions.q: What does 'data at rest' refer to?
options: Data stored on disk, as opposed to data actively moving over a network
Data that has been permanently deleted
Data stored only in RAM
Data that is currently being typed into a form
questions.explain: Data at rest is data sitting on storage media — exactly what's exposed if a drive is removed from a stolen machine.

questions.q: Why doesn't a Windows login password protect a stolen laptop's data on its own?
options: The drive can be removed and read directly on another machine, bypassing the login screen entirely
Login passwords encrypt the entire drive automatically
Login passwords are stored on a separate, unrelated drive
Windows login passwords expire after 24 hours
questions.explain: Pulling the drive and mounting it elsewhere skips the login prompt completely, leaving unencrypted data fully readable.

questions.q: What makes BitLocker 'full-disk' encryption rather than file-level encryption?
options: Once enabled, it encrypts the entire volume — OS, applications, files, and free space — not just selected files or folders
It only encrypts files larger than 1 GB
It encrypts one folder at a time, chosen by the user
It only applies to removable USB drives
questions.explain: BitLocker protects the whole volume at once, so there's no folder an administrator could forget to include.

questions.q: What role does the TPM play in BitLocker?
options: It stores the encryption key in hardware and validates boot integrity before releasing that key
It replaces the need for a recovery key entirely
It only functions when the machine is connected to the internet
It encrypts data over the network, not on disk
questions.explain: The TPM holds the key separately from the drive and checks that boot components haven't been tampered with before releasing it.

questions.q: Why does BitLocker generate a 48-digit recovery key when encryption is enabled?
options: Because the TPM can legitimately withhold the normal key (firmware change, forgotten PIN, tampering), and the recovery key is the backup way to unlock the drive
Because the recovery key is required every single time the machine boots
Because BitLocker cannot function without entering it daily
Because it replaces the Windows login password
questions.explain: The recovery key is stored separately so the drive remains recoverable even if the TPM won't release its key through the normal path.
